learning: Iteration 0 showed max error of 0.063 to 0.066 m with low RMS and high oscillation, so the limit was breached by transients, not offset. Watch whether max_error on bends falls below 0.06 m and whether steering_oscillation drops from 0.11 to 0.16.
notes: Adopts the Builder's iteration 1 geometry unchanged and retunes the controller for the lower mass, narrower track and larger sensors. kp is cut from 0.8 to 0.6 and kd from 0.15 to 0.10 to reduce overshoot and jitter.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the baseline on all three development tracks, and every one of the 60 runs ended off track with no finishes. RMS error was small (0.019 to 0.032 m), but max error reached 0.063 to 0.066 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Steering oscillation was high (0.11 to 0.16) and progress was low (0.12 to 0.20). That pattern points to large transient excursions on bends, with jitter, rather than a steady offset. The Builder's iteration 1 geometry changes the robot's dynamics in three ways: 0.6 kg mass lowers yaw inertia, so the robot responds faster and can overshoot more; a 0.10 m wheel track gives about 20 percent more turn rate per unit of PWM difference, so the effective steering gain rises; and the 16 mm sensors on a ±0.02 m array give a stronger signal per metre of offset than the 12 mm, ±0.024 m array. Together these mean the old kp of 0.8 is likely too aggressive. I reduce kp from 0.8 to 0.6 to offset the higher effective gain. I reduce kd from 0.15 to 0.10 because the steering oscillation metric is jitter, and a derivative term acting on the 16 mm signal amplifies it. I keep ki at 0 because iteration 0 gave no evidence that a steady offset exists, so integral windup has no benefit yet. I keep base_speed at 1.5 because the robot must average about 1.5 m/s to finish in 3 s, and a slower run cannot complete. The sensor weights stay at [-2,-1,0,1,2] because the sensor x-positions are still in the same order and the array remains symmetric. The line_loss setting stays last_direction. Expected result, not yet measured: lower peak error on bends and lower oscillation, with the first finishes possible on the oval and s-bend. The next race should show whether the remaining excursions come from lag or saturation.
